claims.text: Successful formation of noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles is governed by the relative atomic diffusion rates of the constituent elements during synthesis.
Sufficiently similar diffusion rates promote homogeneous alloying.
Sharply different diffusion rates promote phase separation or elemental segregation.
The proposed starting material contains five or more noble-metal precursors, exemplified by Pt, Pd, Ir, Rh, and Ru.
Changing the constituent elements while holding rapid thermal-processing conditions constant provides a controlled comparison of relative diffusion behavior.
Closely matched diffusion rates allow the constituent atoms to intermix efficiently before phase separation or decomposition occurs.
Efficient atomic intermixing produces homogeneous HEA nanoparticles.
Homogeneous HEA nanoparticle formation resulting from matched diffusion rates preserves substantial surface-atom exposure.
When diffusion rates differ significantly, faster-diffusing elements segregate or form separate phases.
Diffusion-rate disparities can lead to non-uniform nanoparticle morphology.
Samples with disparate constituent diffusion rates will have lower surface-atom exposure than samples with closely matched rates.
The proposed diffusion-rate mechanism applies to noble metal–based HEA nanoparticles made by rapid thermal processing or similar methods in which diffusion kinetics dominate.
The mechanism does not apply when chemical reduction, templating, or surfactant-mediated assembly overrides diffusion-driven mixing.
The mechanism does not apply to non-noble-metal HEAs having fundamentally different bonding or melting behavior.
The threshold defining sufficiently similar diffusion rates may depend on synthesis conditions.
Precursor chemistry and atmosphere may also influence alloy formation.
Formation of homogeneous, high-surface-exposure nanoparticles from sharply mismatched diffusion-rate elements would falsify the hypothesis.
Phase separation among elements with closely matched diffusion rates would falsify the hypothesis.
